entries.title: Job 33:3
segments: Clearly; purely, with sincerity, as the original word implies.

entries.title: Job 33:4
segments: Hath made--given me life; hath made me a man endowed with reason. See note to

entries.title: Job 33:5
segments: If we cannot justify ourselves before frail sinful men like ourselves, much less can we before the omniscient, heart-searching, rein-trying God; and we should not attempt it, but confess and forsake our sins and turn heartily to him that we may find mercy.

entries.title: Job 33:6
segments: In God's stead; he would speak for God, and attempt to justify him in his dealings with Job.

entries.title: Job 33:7
segments: My terror--my hand; he refers to Job's words,

entries.title: Job 33:9
segments: I am innocent; Job meant, that he was innocent of the crimes with which his friends charged him; but Elihu interpreted what he had said, to mean that he was free from all sin.

entries.title: Job 33:10
segments:
He; God. 
 
Great care should be taken, that in our distresses we do not seem to reflect upon the righteousness, wisdom, or goodness of God; or attribute to him, even in thought or feeling, any thing derogatory to his holy and perfect character.

entries.title: Job 33:11
segments: He putteth my feet in the stocks; shuts me up to great calamities.

entries.title: Job 33:12
segments: Thou art not just; in thus speaking of God as if he were unjust and cruel.

entries.title: Job 33:14
segments: For God speaketh; though God will not allow himself to be arraigned for his dealings at any human tribunal, yet he graciously reveals his will to the humble and teachable, by night visions,
; and by fatherly chastisement,
.  They who will attend to these admonitions shall be restored to God's favor and their former prosperity,
.  Such is the course of Elihu's argument.

entries.title: Job 33:16
segments: Sealeth their instruction; impresses instruction upon their minds and hearts, as to the consequences of virtue and vice.

entries.title: Job 33:17
segments:
His purpose; his purpose of committing iniquity. 
 
  Hide pride from man; make him humble. 
 
God addresses men in a great variety of ways, sometimes in mercies and sometimes in trials; but his object is to humble them for their sins, lead them to repentance, and thus prepare them for his everlasting love.

entries.title: Job 33:18
segments: He keepeth back; or, that he may keep back; for this verse expresses the end for which God instructs men in visions of the night.

entries.title: Job 33:19
segments: He is chastened; Elihu here names the second way in which God impresses instruction upon man, namely, by visiting him with sickness, and in various ways afflicting him, not for his destruction, but for his profit.

entries.title: Job 33:22
segments: To the destroyers; the ministers of death, whether in the form of diseases or of destroying angels.

entries.title: Job 33:23
segments:
A messenger--an interpreter; a messenger sent to the man in his affliction to interpret to him its meaning, and show him his duty in regard to it.  Some understand here a heavenly messenger, that is, an angel; others, an earthly messenger.  The last interpretation is favored by the words, "one among a thousand," which imply that among men such a wise expounder of God's will is rarely to be found. 
 
  To show unto man his uprightness; to show him the uprightness or righteousness of God in his afflictions, that they are designed to lead him to repentance, and thus prepare him for a renewal and increase of blessings. 
 
The great and effectual teacher as to the righteousness of God in all his dispensations, and the sinfulness of men, is the Holy Spirit; and if a man receives his teaching and obeys it, God will be gracious to him, overrule his trials for his good, and through the ransom which He has provided, save him with an everlasting salvation.

entries.title: Job 33:24
segments: Then he is gracious; then, when he repents and acknowledges God's uprightness, God will be gracious to  the penitent, and deliver him from death through the ransom or atonement he has provided.

entries.title: Job 33:25
segments: His flesh shall be fresher than a child's; he shall be restored to perfect health, and put on again the freshness and vigor of youth.

entries.title: Job 33:26
segments: The humble and penitent soul has access to God by prayer and supplication; and he receives gracious answers of peace, and is ripening, under all the dispensations of Providence, for complete deliverance from sin, and an entrance into that rest which remaineth for the people of God.

entries.title: Job 33:27
segments:
vv 27-28. 
 
  He looketh upon men--shall see the light; of this passage there are two readings, one given by our translators in the text, the other thus: "He [the restored penitent] shall look upon men, and say, I have sinned, and perverted right, and it profited me not.  He hath delivered my soul from going into the pit, and my life sees the light." 
 
  If any say, I have sinned; repent of and forsake his sins. 
 
  See the light; be visited with prosperity.

entries.title: Job 33:30
segments: To bring back his soul from the pit; the general doctrine of Elihu was, that the Lord sends afflictions to bring men to repentance, and thus to save them from death and fit them for the blessings of his grace.
